AllenRelation.description:
Allen's thirteen interval relations, recorded as a parameter on ``succeeds``.

Files and sessions have extents, not only instants, and "overlaps" is
different evidence from "before". These are parameters on an existing
primitive rather than primitives of their own: they qualify an ordering, they
do not constitute a new kind of relationship.

``DURING`` and ``CONTAINS_INTERVAL`` are Allen's *during* and *contains*. The
second is spelled out to keep it clearly distinct from the ``contains``
primitive, which is filesystem containment and unrelated.
AllenRelation.title: AllenRelation

ClockKind.description:
Which clock a time-consuming rule reads.

Exposed as a rule parameter so a user can see and change which clock a
conclusion rests on, rather than discovering it by reading code.
ClockKind.title: ClockKind

DecisionStatus.description: The standing of an assertion in the published graph.
DecisionStatus.title: DecisionStatus

Defeater.description:
A recorded reason a claim would be retracted.

Defeasible and abductive claims must be able to name what would defeat them.
A defeater is a visible event: evidence either raises a claim's tier, leaves
it unchanged, or introduces one of these. It never quietly erodes a score.
Defeater.title: Defeater

ExpansionState.description:
Why the engine stopped expanding a container. Required on every ``embeds``.

This field is what makes the absence of an embedding edge readable. Without
it, "the archive holds nothing else" and "the engine did not look far enough"
are the same silence, and a closed-world statement could rest on the second.
ExpansionState.title: ExpansionState

InferenceTier.description:
The kind of reasoning that produced a claim.

Four kinds, and the differences between them are differences in what could
make the claim wrong, which is why they are a vocabulary rather than a
number.
InferenceTier.title: InferenceTier

Primitive.description: The eight relation primitives. The set is closed.
Primitive.title: Primitive

QuotientOrigin.description:
Whether an edge at a coarse level was lifted from below or asserted there.

Some relationships exist only at a coarse level and have no fine-grained
counterpart: two sets of experiments relate within a month while their movie
files relate within a day. A model that only lifts cannot express that, so
rules may attach to a level and assert natively at it.
QuotientOrigin.title: QuotientOrigin

ReferenceResolution.description:
How well a reference string resolved. Recorded on every ``references``.

These are not interchangeable, and keeping them apart is what lets the engine
say "this script claims to write that file, and that file does not exist",
which is a finding rather than an error.
ReferenceResolution.title: ReferenceResolution

Scope.description:
Where a rule, assertion or decision applies.

Scope is first-class because the most common real correction is not "this
rule is wrong" but "this rule is wrong *here*". Without scoping, a user
disables a good rule globally in order to fix one folder.
Scope.title: Scope

ScopeKind.description: The kind of region a rule, an assertion or a decision applies to.
ScopeKind.title: ScopeKind

SupportComponent.description:
One named piece of positive support for a candidate or a claim.

Components are kept as a vector and never summed into a scalar before the
decision is made. Summation is what triple-counts one underlying fact seen
three ways, and it is why ``family`` exists: components sharing a family are
views of one fact and must not compound with each other.
SupportComponent.title: SupportComponent

description:
A published edge.

Identity derives from source, target, primitive, respect, rule, rule version
and scope, and from nothing else. The evidence that justified the edge lives
in the fields below, beside the identifier rather than inside it, so evidence
can be revised without the edge becoming a different edge.
title: Assertion
